process_area.title: Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle

fields.Participants: Domain owners (ABC/privacy/cyber/ESG/financial), Procurement (VS-03), Legal (VS-100.3), business owners
fields.Trigger: New Critical/High third party; periodic re-DD; material change
fields.Volume: ~80–120 Critical/High third parties (deepest DD); ~300–500 Medium (standard); remainder Low (light)

workflows.name: Risk-Based Due Diligence Library & Assessment Workflow (Pre-Contract & Periodic)

Automation Opportunity: - Tier-driven DD pack assembly; vendor portal for DD response; findings-to-tiering integration
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: tier-driven DD applied; findings feed tiering; high-residual risk formally accepted; evidence retained
Cross-references: - links to W4722/W4723 (appetite/tiering), W4730–W4733 (domain DD), W4727 (financial/ESG), VS-88 (records)
Pain Points / Risks: - **DD-fatigue risk**: Same DD requested redundantly by each domain → vendor fatigue and inconsistent conclusions; mitigated by the unified DD library
- **Risk-acceptance-untracked risk**: High-residual risk accepted informally → unmanaged; mitigated by documented risk acceptance per appetite
System Touchpoints: - TPRM platform (DD library/workflow); domain-owner systems; procurement (VS-03); records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain the risk-based DD library: tier-driven DD packs (Critical/High = full cross-domain DD; Medium = standard; Low = light), each combining the domain-specific DD (cyber W4730, privacy W4731, ABC W4732, resilience W4733, financial/ESG W4727)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Run the DD assessment workflow per third party pre-contract and periodically: issue the pack, collect responses/evidence, score, and feed findings into tiering (W4723) and contract terms
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Domain Owners / Procurement

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Document DD conclusions and residual risk; obtain risk acceptance for high-residual third parties per the appetite (W4722); retain evidence (VS-88)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

fields.Frequency: Per third party + annual attestation refresh
fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with Cyber VS-27.3)
fields.Participants: Cyber (VS-27.3 W367), IT (VS-27), Privacy (VS-91), the third party
fields.Trigger: New IT/SaaS/payment third party; attestation expiry; cyber DD
fields.Volume: ~80–150 IT/SaaS/cloud/payment/marketplace third parties handling data or integrated to BuildRight systems

workflows.name: Cybersecurity & IT-Controls Attestation (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / PCI DSS) Collection

Automation Opportunity: - Attestation repository with scope-mapping; expiry-alerts; gap-remediation tracking
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: attestation appropriate to data/risk; scope reviewed; gaps remediated; refresh tracked (W4735)
Cross-references: - extends VS-27.3 W367 (cyber-vendor governance); links to VS-113 (integration), VS-91 (privacy), W4735 (renewal), W4736 (incidents)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attestation-scope-mismatch risk**: A SOC 2 that doesn't cover the service BuildRight uses → false assurance; mitigated by scope review
- **Unremediated-gap risk**: A cyber gap not remediated → breach exposure; mitigated by remediation/compensating-control requirement
System Touchpoints: - Cyber (VS-27.3 W367); attestation repository; IT integration risk (VS-27/VS-113); records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / CIO
steps.activity: For each IT/SaaS/payment third party, collect cybersecurity & IT-controls attestation appropriate to the data/risk: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS (for payment data), or a security questionnaire for lower-tier; extend enterprise-wide the cyber-vendor slice in VS-27.3 W367

steps.a: TPRM Lead / CIO
steps.activity: Review the attestation for coverage and gaps (scope, exceptions, qualified opinions); require remediation/compensating controls for gaps; coordinate with cyber (VS-27.3) on penetration-test/monitoring integration

steps.a: TPRM Lead / CIO
steps.activity: Track attestation expiry and refresh (W4735); manage third-party cyber incidents (W4736) and integration-risk (VS-27.3/VS-113); retain evidence (VS-88)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with Privacy/DPO VS-91)
fields.Participants: Privacy/DPO (VS-91.2 W3052), Legal (VS-100.3), Cyber (VS-27.3), the third party
fields.Trigger: New data-handling third party; privacy review (VS-91); sub-processor change
fields.Volume: ~80–150 data-handling third parties (SaaS, BPO, payment, marketplace, CDP/fraud)

workflows.name: Data-Privacy & Processor Due Diligence (DPA, Transfer Mechanism)

Automation Opportunity: - DPA/template library; sub-processor-change workflow; DPIA integration (VS-91.2)
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: DPA in place before data handling; transfer mechanism valid; sub-processor changes managed; extends W3052
Cross-references: - extends VS-91.2 W3052 (data-processor oversight); links to W4724 (fourth party), W4740 (exit data-return), VS-91 (privacy program)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-DPA risk**: A processor handling personal data without a DPA → RA 10173 violation; mitigated by mandatory DPA before data handling
- **Cross-border-transfer risk**: Personal data transferred abroad without a valid mechanism → violation; mitigated by transfer-mechanism assessment
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/DPIA (VS-91.2 W3052); contracts (VS-100.3); cyber (VS-27.3); records (VS-88); TPRM platform

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO
steps.activity: For each data-handling third party, conduct privacy & processor DD: Data Processing Agreement (DPA), purpose limitation, sub-processor disclosure (W4724), cross-border transfer mechanism (vs. Philippine DPA RA 10173 and destination law), data-subject-rights support, breach-notification obligations — extends VS-91.2 W3052 enterprise-wide

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO / VP Legal
steps.activity: Coordinate Privacy Impact Assessment (VS-91.2 DPIA) for high-risk data processing; ensure the DPA covers BuildRight's obligations (VS-91) and the processor's; manage cross-border transfers

steps.a: TPRM Lead / DPO
steps.activity: Monitor sub-processor changes (a processor adding a fourth party per VS-91.2 W3052 requires notice/objection); manage privacy incidents (W4736) and data-return/deletion on exit (W4740)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with ABC/AML VS-86)
fields.Participants: ABC/AML (VS-86.3 W2942), Legal (VS-100.3), Compliance (VS-22), screening provider
fields.Trigger: New third party; ABC risk (VS-86); sanctions watch-list refresh
fields.Volume: ~ all third parties (sanctions); ~ higher-risk for ABC (intermediaries, government-facing)

Automation Opportunity: - Continuous sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening; beneficial-ownership workflow; hit-management tooling
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: continuous sanctions screening; beneficial-ownership identified; EDD for high-risk; extends W2942
Cross-references: - extends VS-86.3 W2942 (ABC DD); links to VS-46/VS-104 (government-facing), W4723 (tiering), VS-100.3 (contracts)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sanctions-hit-miss risk**: A sanctions hit not detected → regulatory/ reputational exposure; mitigated by continuous screening
- **Hidden-beneficial-owner risk**: A sanctioned party hidden behind ownership layers; mitigated by beneficial-ownership identification
System Touchpoints: - ABC/AML (VS-86.3 W2942); sanctions-screening platform; contracts (VS-100.3); records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / VP Legal
steps.activity: For each third party, conduct ABC/sanctions/beneficial-ownership DD: sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening (continuous), beneficial-ownership identification, and ABC DD scaled to risk (intermediaries, government-facing VS-46/VS-104) — extends VS-86.3 W2942 enterprise-wide

steps.a: TPRM Lead / VP Legal
steps.activity: Apply enhanced DD for high-risk third parties (government-facing, high-risk geographies, complex ownership); require anti-bribery certifications and flow-downs in contracts

steps.a: TPRM Lead / VP Legal
steps.activity: Manage screening hits (true vs. false positive) per VS-86; manage ongoing screening changes (ownership change, new adverse media); feed findings into tiering (W4723)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager (joint with BCP VS-26)
fields.Participants: BCP (VS-26), Supply (VS-02.3), IT/DR (VS-27.2 W55), business owners, the third party
fields.Trigger: New Critical third party; BCP review (VS-26); periodic refresh
fields.Volume: ~40–60 Critical third parties whose failure would disrupt operations

workflows.name: Operational, Resilience & BCP/DR Evidence Collection (RTO/RPO, Substitutes)

Automation Opportunity: - Resilience-evidence repository; RTO/RPO-vs-requirement matching; test-result tracking
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: Critical third-party BCP/DR evidence collected; RTO/RPO meets BuildRight requirements; tested jointly (W4738); extends W1328/W334
Cross-references: - extends VS-21.2 W1328/W334; links to VS-26 (BCP), VS-02.3 (supply disruption), VS-27.2 W55 (IT DR), W4738 (testing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-resilience-assurance risk**: A third party's BCP claim not tested → failure in a real event; mitigated by evidence and joint testing (W4738)
- **RTO-mismatch risk**: A third party's RTO longer than BuildRight can tolerate → disruption; mitigated by the RTO/RPO assessment
System Touchpoints: - BCP (VS-26); supply disruption (VS-02.3 W729); IT DR (VS-27.2 W55); resilience testing (W4738); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~per Critical third party 1–2 days evidence collection

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: For each Critical third party, collect operational-resilience & BCP/DR evidence: the third party's BCP/DR plan, RTO/RPO, recovery-site, dependency on its own fourth parties (W4724), substitute availability, and recent test results — extends VS-21.2 W1328/W334 enterprise-wide

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / COO
steps.activity: Assess whether the third party's RTO/RPO meets BuildRight's requirements (operations continuity, VS-26); require gaps be remediated or compensating resilience (alternate source W4737, safety stock)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Coordinate resilience testing (joint exercise W4738); integrate third-party BCP into BuildRight's BCP (VS-26) and supply-chain disruption response (VS-02.3 W729); retain evidence (VS-88)

fields.Participants: Cyber (VS-27.3), Financial (Treasury VS-18/SCF VS-105), ABC (VS-86), performance owners (VS-67)

workflows.name: Continuous Monitoring Platform: Financial, Cyber, Compliance, Performance Feed

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated monitoring platform; alert-triage workflow; re-DD auto-trigger
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: Critical/High continuously monitored; alerts triaged; material changes escalate to tiering/DD; monitoring lawful
Cross-references: - links to W4723 (tiering), W4729 (re-DD), W4732 (ABC), W4735 (cert), VS-67 (performance), W4743 (KRIs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Alert-fatigue risk**: High alert volume without triage → real signals missed; mitigated by tuned thresholds and domain-triage
- **Point-in-time-DD-only risk**: DD done once at onboarding and never refreshed → stale risk view; mitigated by continuous monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Continuous-monitoring platform; financial/cyber/compliance/performance feeds; domain-owner systems; records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Operate the continuous-monitoring platform: feeds of financial health (credit/financials), cyber posture (breach news, rating services), compliance (sanctions/adverse-media W4732, certifications W4735), and performance (SLA/scorecard VS-67) for Critical/High third parties

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Triage alerts (financial deterioration, breach, sanctions hit, SLA breach, news event); escalate material changes to the tiering (W4723) and domain slices; trigger re-DD (W4729) where warranted

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain monitoring within data/legal bounds (VS-91/VS-100.3); retain intelligence (VS-88); report monitoring KRIs (W4743)

fields.Participants: Cyber (VS-27.3), Insurance (VS-26), Legal (VS-100.3), Procurement (VS-03), the third parties

workflows.name: Attestation, Certification & Insurance (COI) Renewal Tracking Lifecycle

Automation Opportunity: - Renewal calendar with automated alerts; attestation/COI repository; lapse-detection with contract suspension
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: renewal calendar with alerts; lapses managed (suspend/risk-accept/remediate); coverage changes reviewed
Cross-references: - links to W4730 (cyber attestation), VS-26 (insurance/COI), VS-31/VS-117 (quality/DTI-BPS), VS-98 (contingent COI), W4734 (monitoring)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapsed-attestation/COI risk**: A third party operating with lapsed coverage → uninsured/unassured exposure; mitigated by the renewal calendar and lapse-management
- **Coverage-gap risk**: A renewed COI with reduced coverage; mitigated by scope-change review
System Touchpoints: - Renewal calendar (TPRM platform); cyber (VS-27.3); insurance (VS-26); contracts (VS-100.3); records (VS-88)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Maintain the attestation/certification/COI renewal calendar: cyber attestation (W4730), quality/cert (VS-31/VS-117 DTI-BPS), insurance/COI (liability, cyber, workers-comp per VS-26/VS-98), and licenses; alert before expiry

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Collect refreshed attestations/COIs before expiry; review for coverage/scope changes; require remediation for lapsed/expired items; manage contracts that require current attestation/COI
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Cyber / Insurance / Legal

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Manage third parties operating with lapsed attestation/COI (suspend, risk-accept, or remediate); retain evidence (VS-88); feed lapses into monitoring (W4734) and tiering (W4723)

fields.Owner: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
fields.Participants: Cyber IR (VS-27.3 W383), Privacy (VS-91), BCP (VS-26), Fraud (VS-125), Legal (VS-100.3), business owners, the third party
fields.Trigger: Third-party incident (cyber breach, financial failure, operational outage, compliance breach, performance degradation)
fields.Volume: ~25–50 incidents/year across the third-party base (mostly minor lapses)

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-intake workflow; cross-domain response coordination; breach-notification-deadline tracking
Controls: - CTL-714 (ensure controlled execution — Due Diligence, Continuous Monitoring & Evidence Lifecycle (PA-161.2).)
- CTL-714: third-party incidents triaged and managed per domain; notification deadlines met (VS-91); post-incident lessons captured
Cross-references: - links to VS-27.3 W383 (cyber IR), VS-91 (privacy breach), VS-26 (BCP), VS-125 (fraud), W4728 (ownership/board), W4740 (termination)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-incident-detection risk**: A third-party breach detected late → enlarged impact and missed notification deadlines (NPC 72-hour); mitigated by continuous monitoring (W4734) and breach-notification clauses
- **Accountability-vacuum risk**: A third-party incident with no clear BuildRight owner → uncoordinated response; mitigated by the ownership matrix (W4728)
System Touchpoints: - Cyber IR (VS-27.3 W383); privacy breach (VS-91); BCP (VS-26); fraud (VS-125); legal (VS-100); board (W4728)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Intake and triage third-party incidents: cyber breach (coordinate VS-27.3 W383), privacy breach (VS-91 72-hour notification), operational outage (VS-26 BCP activation), financial failure (supply disruption VS-02.3), compliance breach (VS-22), performance degradation (VS-67)

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / VP Legal
steps.activity: Manage incident response: activate BuildRight's response per the affected domain, demand the third party's incident response, assess BuildRight impact (data/operations/customers), and coordinate notification (regulators, customers, board W4728) as required
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Domain Owners / Legal

steps.a: TPRM Lead / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Conduct post-incident review; capture lessons; adjust tiering (W4723), DD (W4729), monitoring (W4734), and contracts; manage third-party accountability (remediation, credit, termination W4740)
steps.r: TPRM Program Manager / Head of Internal Audit & Risk / Legal
